name: Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi
style: Spanish Colonial Revival / Churrigueresque (basilica); adobe mission (chapel)
history: Franciscan friars Francisco Palóu and Pedro Benito Cambón founded the mission on 9 October 1776. Ohlone workers made 36,000 adobe bricks for the chapel, begun in 1788 and finished by 1791; it is the oldest intact building in San Francisco. A brick parish church of 1876 beside it was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake, and the present basilica was built in 1918. Pius XII named it a basilica in 1952.
arch: Two buildings side by side: the small whitewashed adobe chapel with redwood roof beams and a ceiling painted in Ohlone designs, and the ornate twin-towered basilica.
features: The cemetery is the oldest in San Francisco, with the unmarked graves of about 5,000 Native Californians, many Ohlone.
St. Junípero Serra is recorded as saying Mass in the chapel while it was still being built.

look.d: Built by Ohlone hands by 1791, it survived the 1906 earthquake.
The basilica replaced the brick church the 1906 earthquake destroyed.

fun: The name Dolores comes from a nearby creek, Arroyo de Nuestra Señora de los Dolores.
journal: San Francisco's oldest building stands beside a basilica. The adobe outlasted the earthquake.
